question: In the physical examination of a PLHIV, the oral cavity must be examined routinely in every consultation regardless of the presenting complaint, because oral lesions are reliable clinical markers of immunosuppression stage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Oral lesions (candidiasis, hairy leukoplakia, Kaposi sarcoma, aphthous ulcers) are direct windows into immune status and HIV stage. The oral examination must not be omitted.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Oral examination is mandatory in every HIV consultation. Oral candidiasis indicates CD4 < 200 cells/μL; oral hairy leukoplakia is pathognomonic of HIV; and Kaposi sarcoma lesions can appear on the palate — all are accessible markers that change clinical staging.
